messages:
tara: quick gating check — ran a focused perf sweep for FlashAttention v3 + paged-attn + fused kernels against master on redwood/llama-7b. results attached (short summary below). need decision on ff rollout windows and whether to enable adaptive-batching KV heuristic by default.

tara: TL;DR: mean token cost -6% overall, p50 latency -8%, p99 unchanged at short seq (<512), but p99 +12% for long seqs (>2048) during cold-kv misses. KV miss rate spiked on synthetic replay workload (see logs).

kevin: can you paste the key numbers? particularly p99 and tokens/sec across seq bins.

tara: sure — from the profiling run (2000 queries, 8xA100):
```
seq<=512: tokens/sec +9%, p50  -10%, p99  -3%
512<seq<=2048: tokens/sec +5%, p50  -7%, p99  -1%
seq>2048: tokens/sec +2%, p50  -4%, p99 +12% (KV cold miss)
mem overhead: +1.8% (KV paging buffers)
```

sam: interesting. that p99 bump at long sequences smells like paging writes on KV miss causing stalls. did you run with the new async-kv-io path?

tara: yes, async-kv-io=on and async-prefetch heuristic enabled. but our simulated replay had intentionally low locality so misses were common. in normal traffic (prod traces replay) kv-miss-rate ~0.6% -> p99 stable. synthetic worst-case -> 5.4% -> regression shows up.

anita: from OSS flashattn-v3 notes, fused kernel reduces kernel launches but can increase contiguous memory pressure for very long kv caches. could be allocator churn. did you see CUDA allocator spikes?

tara: allocator profiles show 3x increase in short-lived allocations during long seq runs. attaching flame summary link: https://redwood.internal/bench/1912345678-flame (internal).

dana: safety question: if we roll to hosted customers, how do we avoid hitting the long-seq regressions? propose feature-flag split: ff_flash_v3 = global toggle (off default), ff_flash_v3_models = allowlist per-model, ff_flash_v3_long_seq_guard = threshold-based fallback. rollout plan: 1) enable for canary tenant + dedicated-dev 2) 10% traffic for allowlist models 3) monitor 24h -> 50% -> 100%.

kevin: +1 on the guard. we should implement a runtime check: if seq_len > LONG_SEQ_THRESHOLD OR kv_miss_rate > X then route to flashv2/fallback kernel. runtime config names: "LONG_SEQ_THRESHOLD" (default 2048), "KV_MISS_FALLBACK_RATIO" (default 0.02).

tara: added a small patch that tracks kv-miss-rate per-req and emits metric runtime.kv.miss_rate (per-model, per-cluster). telemetry-bot: please confirm metric hooks?

telemetry-bot: hooked: runtime.kv.miss_rate, runtime.flashv3.fallback_count, runtime.flashv3.latency.p99. Alerts: alerted when fallback_count > 0.5% traffic in 5m or p99 increase > 10% over baseline.

anita: also flag for adaptive-batching: our batched_kv_prefetch option currently enables prefetch for any batch size > 1. propose heuristic: if avg_batch_tokens < 256 then prefetch=false to avoid unnecessary IO. otherwise prefetch=true.

sam: small ops note — enabling async-kv-io requires a kernel env var and a driver upgrade for A100 older firmware; ops timeline?

devops-bot: ops note: driver roll for dedicated-prod scheduled Mon 03/30 02:00-04:00 UTC. will coordinate canary window.

kevin: given all that, my recommendation: gate FlashAttention v3 behind ff_flash_v3 (off by default). enable for redwood/llama-7b and redwood/llama-13b on dedicated-dev and hosted-canary tenant at 10% traffic with LONG_SEQ_THRESHOLD=2048 and KV_MISS_FALLBACK_RATIO=0.02, adaptive-batching heuristic as an opt-in flag ff_flashv3_adaptive_batch=true. monitor for 48 hours. rollback criteria: fallback_count > 1% sustained for 5m OR p99 increase > 10% in any seq bin OR error-rate rise > 0.1%.

tara: I'll create the rollout checklist and the FF entries. sample admin command to enable for model:
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/api/flags/enable \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"flag":"ff_flash_v3_models","models":["redwood/llama-7b"],"percentage":10}'
```

dana: please also add a dashboard tile for kv-miss-rate heatmap vs seq_len and include this in the canary runbook.

tara: noted — will add dashboard and pull in oncall for 2hr overlap during canary.

kevin: +:thumbsup: fine by me. any objections?

anita: no objections. also file a follow-up perf task to 1) reduce allocator churn 2) try a pooled allocator for kv pages.

sam: tagging infra: @dana can you confirm capacity impact if we leave paged-attn on for 50% traffic?

dana: rough estimate: memory headroom drops ~3% on p50 load for large models; no immediate capacity emergency but keep an eye. will add autoscaler playbook note.

tara: ok moving forward with the plan. I'll post the rollout doc + checklist in #eng-runtime and create the FF entries. thanks all. :rocket:

telemetry-bot: note: canary run metric baseline captured at 1912330000. comparing windows will auto-populate in the dashboard.
